Let’s reason through this.  

The letter from 1847 expresses concern that Japan’s “antiquated systems” will leave it vulnerable to foreign powers with modern steamships, armies, and weapons.  
Historically, this was the late Tokugawa period, before the Meiji Restoration (1868). In 1853–54, Commodore Perry’s arrival forced Japan to open ports.  
After internal turmoil, the Meiji Restoration began in 1868, and Japan responded by modernizing — sending missions to study Western industry, government, and military systems.  

Option (C) fits: sending emissaries to study western democracies and industry was part of Japan’s modernization in the Meiji era, directly addressing the concerns Lord Ii raised.  

(A) is wrong — dismantling the Chinese-style civil service system was part of modernization but not the main or initial response; also Japan didn’t have exactly the same system as China.  
(B) is wrong — conquest in the Pacific came later, after industrialization.  
(D) is wrong — turning inward was the earlier Sakoku policy; after 1850s Japan opened and modernized.  

Final answer: (C)
